text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.

LONDON - London's FTSE 100 share index rebounded after two days of decline to end higher on Tuesday, rescued by a rejuvenated Dow that charged ahead after weaker-than-expected U.S. wage inflation figures. The FTSE closed 25.4 points higher at 4,237.4, carried up by a buoyant Dow which was 93 points higher as London closed.

FRANKFURT - German DAX index ends down 0.17 percent, in middle of narrow nine-point day's range, as market continues to seek direction amid consolidation after recent record highs. The 30-share DAX ended down 5.20 points at 2,989.33. In post-bourse trade the index stood at 3,028.27 up 35.72.

PARIS - French stocks rose to close at a record high on Tuesday, boosted by market-friendly U.S. economic data which lowered fears of a U.S. interest rate hike and lifted debt markets in the United States and Europe. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 47.59 points or 1.95 percent at 2,482.76.

ZURICH - Soaring pharmaceutical shares lifted Swiss share indices by more than one percent to a record close in high volumes. Dealers said the U.S. employment cost index, which was below market expectations, and the firming U.S. dollar also gave shares a boost. The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 34.16 points, or 1.29 percent, to close at 2,676.67.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks bounced back on Tuesday and closed higher for the first time in four days. The recent falls sparked bargain-hunting in global blue-chip issues which started to become more attractive, such as Fujitsu Ltd and Sony Corp, The key Nikkei 225 average finished up 461.67 points, or 2.66 percent, at 17,796.57.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks finished strong on Tuesday, rebounding after five straight losing sessions and spurred by talk that CITIC Pacific may buy a stake in China Light and Power. The Hang Seng Index rose 108.39 points, or 0.82 percent, to 13,403.29.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market closed lower on Tuesday after the Dow continued its downtrend. The only local bright spot was a gold sector that received a pick-me-up from a firmer bullion price in offshore markets. The All Ordinaries index lost 18.8 points to close at 2,404.2.

JOHANNESBURG - Life breathed into South African industrials towards close as stocks bounce into positive territory after weakness all day on expectations of a strong U.S. market on Tuesday. Golds buoyant, index up almost 4.0 pct on bullion's rise, but stocks off day's best levels as metal dips below $356. All-share index up 47.0 points at 6,736.0, golds gain 54.1 to 1,429.4 and industrials up 25.1 to 8,069.0.
